context_length: T5 relative position bias; longer sequences are embedded whole here
summary: The full-size Ankh model: a T5 with a 1.15B-parameter encoder and 1536-dim embeddings, reported to outperform larger PLMs of its time with far fewer parameters.
architecture: T5 encoder-decoder with relative position bias, 48 encoder and 24 decoder layers, wider than Ankh-base (1536 vs 768 dims, 16 heads). Only the encoder is used here (1.15B parameters), giving 1536-dim per-residue embeddings.
pretraining_data: UniRef50, trained with JAX/Flax on Google TPU v4 pods.
pretraining_objective: T5-style denoising with 20% of residues masked as single-residue spans, reconstructed by the decoder with the paper's partial demasking.
key_innovations: Reported state-of-the-art general-purpose performance with under 10% of the pretraining parameters of prior PLMs
Recipe chosen through more than twenty pretraining experiments on masking, depth and width
when_to_use: A strong, efficient alternative to ProtT5/ESM-2 for enzyme property prediction; 1536-dim embeddings balance quality and cost.
caveats: Encoder–decoder checkpoint carries unused decoder weights for embedding use; single-sequence, sequence-only.

citations.title: Ankh: Optimized Protein Language Model Unlocks General-Purpose Modelling
